reason:
The kernel finds the top-k cutoff by 40 fixed bisection steps on [row min, row max] (kernel.py lines 13-21) and then keeps every entry >= the resulting `lo`. Because the interval only shrinks by 2^-40 of the row's span, `lo` can remain far below the true k-th largest value, so entries that are neither among the k largest nor tied with the k-th value are kept nonzero -- a direct violation of problem.txt's "out[j] = 0 otherwise" and its hard requirement that "every kept entry is at least as large as every dropped one" (the tie clause covers only entries sharing the k-th value).

What I ran:
- t7 (c1): 12 benign configurations (randn 64x1024 / 8x128, uniform 16x512, softmax(3*randn) 16x512; k=1,5,50) are bitwise equal to the admit-all-ties reference; kept count == k, 0 entries below the cutoff. So the kernel is correct on moderate-dynamic-range rows and the bug is distribution-dependent, which is why a plain random-input allclose test would pass.
- t9/t11 (c2, confirmed): scan over peakedness. Finite softmax probability rows over V=32000 fail once the row spans many decades: logit std 20 -> kept up to 25389 for k=50 with 25343 entries strictly below the k-th largest (worst kept/cutoff ratio 5.8e-33); std 30 -> kept_min 6018; std 40 -> kept_min 1245; temperature 0.1 -> kept up to 9683 with 23163 entries below cutoff. Rows with -inf-masked logits (the standard banned-token mask in top-k sampling) fail totally: kept 32000/32000, -inf itself written into the output (4 and 6344 nonfinite entries), and min(kept) >= max(dropped) is False, while the reference output is finite in every case.
- t14 (c3, confirmed, decisive): re-ran the decisive case with a fixed seed and an explicit `isfinite(p).all()` assertion on the input, so no infinities or out-of-range values are involved. probs = softmax(randn*3/0.1), V=32000, k=50: kept_count_max 10735 (contract requires 50), kept_strictly_below_kth = 52309, worst wrongly-kept value 1.4e-45 against a row cutoff of 3.74e-13 (ratio 3.7e-33), exact_match_ref False. Controls in the same probe (logit std 2 k=50, logit std 20 k=50, logit std 30 k=5) are exact with kept == k and 0 entries below the cutoff, confirming the metric and reference are sound.

Scope: problem.txt is the operative contract, states the formula and the kept>=dropped invariant with no restriction on score magnitudes, and declares the input domain to be the candidate-selection step of top-k sampling whose kept entries are renormalized as sampling weights. Peaked/low-temperature softmax probability rows over a 32k vocabulary are exactly that domain and are ordinary finite float32.

Mitigating note recorded for completeness: in the failing case the downstream renormalized-weight total-variation error is only ~1.1e-12 because the spuriously kept probability mass is tiny, so a tolerance-based comparison of the renormalized distribution would not catch it. The violation is nonetheless of a behaviour the contract states explicitly -- the nonzero candidate set is ~200x too large, entries 33 orders of magnitude below the cutoff are kept, and the -inf-mask case both breaks the kept>=dropped invariant and emits non-finite outputs -- so it is a defect rather than accepted rounding or an admitted tie-breaking choice.
